identity.real_world_identity_notes: Audi specifies the R8 LMS GT4 with a seven-speed dual-clutch S tronic transmission, steering-wheel paddles, and electrohydraulically operated wet multi-plate clutches.

wheel_rim.notes: Audi's exact 2018 technical data calls this a multi-functional steering wheel but does not establish whether the rim has an open top.

notes: With Auto Clutch disabled, AMS2 1.6.9.91 moved the car from rest without physical clutch input, consistent with the manufacturer's electrohydraulically operated dual-clutch architecture.
All seven forward gears were selected by paddles, and clutch-free full-throttle upshifts were accepted with a perceptible automatic cut.
Clutch-free downshifts were accepted with the driver's foot off the throttle, and automatic blip was directly visible as a throttle-display spike.
Live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with Auto Clutch disabled.

Clutch-free move-off, seven paddle-selected gears, no-lift clutch-free upshifts with automatic cut, clutch-free downshifts with automatic blip, and an open-top no-display GT/Formula rim were directly observed.

overrides.condition: AMS2 1.6.9.91 models an open-top GT/Formula rim.

confidence.basis: Direct cockpit inspection during the guided drive.

Audi establishes the R8 LMS GT4 identity and dual-clutch transmission. ACC reported the exact model and GT4 class with stable internal id `audi_r8_gt4`; the guided drive directly established the simulator behavior and cockpit.

claims.basis: Audi's exact 2018 technical data specifies a multi-functional steering wheel but does not describe its top-edge geometry. The 2020 GT2-derived wheel is a later revision and is not inherited backward.
Official addition plus the exact live telemetry name and GT4 class observed through SimHub 9.11.22.
Audi's technical data specifies a seven-speed dual-clutch transmission with steering-wheel paddles, and all seven forward gears were exercised in AMS2.

Direct testing established clutch-free move-off, no-lift clutch-free upshifts with perceptible cut, and clutch-free downshifts with a visible automatic-blip spike; the manufacturer documents automatic electrohydraulic clutch operation.
Direct cockpit inspection showed an open-top GT/Formula rim without an integrated display.

ACC reported telemetry name `Audi R8 LMS GT4 2016`, internal id `audi_r8_gt4`, and class `GT4`. The simulator's 2016 label is retained only as an exact telemetry identity; it does not replace the curated 2018 technical-specification year established by Audi.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.

notes: Simulator behavior and manufacturer hardware evidence agree that no physical clutch pedal action is required for normal use.

The wheel-rim shape was originally recorded as "gt-style". The separate "gt-style", "formula" and "prototype" values described the same rim: molded grips at 9 and 3 with a control face between them, usually carrying a display and rev lights. They are merged into "gt-formula". The rim was not observed again and nothing about the observation changed.
driver_summary: GT4 racer using the road car's dual-clutch gearbox. It cuts the upshift and blips the downshift, and pulls away without a clutch, so the paddles and two pedals are the whole job.
